Microcytic anemia w ↓retic count & ↑RDW ← Fe deficiency

•children: dietary & maternal factors - MC dietary: insuff Fe intake · obesity · unmodified cow’s milk <1y
•pediatric: excessive milk (>24oz/d) · GI bleed · prematurity · maternal Fe deficiency · low-Fe formula · failure to supp breastfed infants
•goat’s milk diet less commonly assoc w IDA - may need vit D supp
•mother’s diet heavy in cheese: may upset stomach of breastfed child - ⍉assoc w IDA
•dietary Fe sources: red meats · beans · dark green leafy vegetables · fortified cereals & breads

•other sources: industrial pollution · occupational or take-home exposure · contaminated soil · drinking H2O from lead service lines · traditional meds & cosmetics · foodware · tobacco · contaminated foods & spices
RF: low-income households · older poorly maintained home · parents exposed @ work - ingestion MC in children (> inhalation)
Children more suscep: rapidly growing bodies · immature organ systems - heme & developing nervous system esp affected
<6y more profoundly affected: incomplete BBB (lead enters nervous system) · crawl on floors · put objects in mouth
Distribution: some cleared in urine & bile - rest binds RBCs → builds up in soft tissues & bone (remains for decades)
Heme: oxidative stress · early RBC death · hemolytic anemia - Neuro: crosses BBB → permanent brain damage · cog defects
May be aSx or nonspecific sxs
-neurobehavioral deficits · hearing loss - affects CNS & PNS · heme synth pathway · kidneys
